summary: Established an AIDE-based file-integrity baseline for /etc on node1 (RHEL 7.9). Installed AIDE (fixed the dead EPEL7 metalink, then installed from the subscribed rhel-7-server-rpms repo), verified the stock RHEL7 aide.conf already gives deep /etc coverage (CONTENT_EX rules for ~80 critical config paths plus a recursive /etc/ PERMS catch-all), initialized the database at /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz, and proved detection works by modifying /etc/hosts (AIDE flagged the SHA256 change) then reverting it back to a clean state. Added /etc/cron.daily/aide-check to automatically run and log daily integrity reports to /var/log/aide/, then re-baselined to include that script itself so the database is fully current and clean. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id and DB checksum baseline, issued a background shutdown -r now so the ack returned before disconnect, polled until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed and uptime reset, then verified the AIDE database checksum was unchanged, aide --check still reports clean, and the cron script/package survived the reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (RHEL 7.9) and confirmed AIDE was not installed
Fixed dead EPEL7 metalink by repointing epel.repo baseurl to archives.fedoraproject.org, then installed aide from the subscribed rhel-7-server-rpms repo
Reviewed /etc/aide.conf and confirmed extensive built-in /etc monitoring rules (per-file CONTENT_EX + recursive /etc/ PERMS catch-all)
Ran aide --init and promoted aide.db.new.gz to aide.db.gz as the baseline
Ran aide --check to confirm a clean baseline
Modified /etc/hosts, re-ran aide --check to confirm detection of the SHA256 diff, then reverted the file and reconfirmed a clean check
Created /etc/cron.daily/aide-check to run daily integrity checks and log reports to /var/log/aide/
Ran the cron script once to validate it works, then re-baselined (aide --update) to fold the new script into the database so the baseline is clean and current
Captured pre-restart boot_id and AIDE db checksum baseline
Issued a backgrounded shutdown -r now on node1 so the acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec access returned
Verified boot_id changed and uptime -s reset, proving an actual restart
Verified post-restart AIDE db checksum unchanged, aide --check clean, cron script and aide package intact

evidence.requirement: AIDE installed and baseline database initialized for /etc
evidence.summary: aide-0.15.1 installed; aide --init created aide.db.new.gz which was promoted to aide.db.gz as the live baseline

evidence.requirement: Baseline config covers /etc with meaningful rules
evidence.summary: aide.conf shows dozens of explicit /etc/* CONTENT_EX rules plus a catch-all /etc/ PERMS rule covering the rest of the tree

evidence.requirement: Baseline is clean/valid immediately after init
evidence.summary: aide --check reports 'All files match AIDE database. Looks okay!' right after initialization

evidence.requirement: Baseline can identify later changes to /etc (core task requirement)
evidence.summary: Appending a line to /etc/hosts caused aide --check to report 'changed: /etc/hosts' with old/new SHA256 hashes, demonstrating change detection

evidence.requirement: Baseline restored to clean state after test
evidence.summary: Reverted the /etc/hosts test edit and confirmed aide --check returns to 'Looks okay!'

evidence.requirement: Automated reporting of future changes is in place
evidence.summary: Created /etc/cron.daily/aide-check; ran it manually and confirmed it produces a dated report log with real AIDE findings

evidence.requirement: Baseline re-synced to include monitoring script itself, final clean state
evidence.summary: aide --update absorbed the new cron script into the database; final aide --check reports fully clean

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline captured for node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 745be096-a20a-49f6-8cb0-9d59222eb06c, AIDE db SHA256 268ddca2..., and a clean aide --check prior to restart
Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' issued; REBOOT_ACK_ISSUED returned to caller before the node dropped

evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Node unreachable mid-reboot (connection timed out), then came back with boot_id 9d4cd30d-4d00-4e8e-a8d4-8ceb0e836c4c, differing from the pre-restart boot_id

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of integrity baseline and services verified
evidence.summary: After restart: uptime -s shows new boot time, AIDE db SHA256 unchanged (268ddca2...), aide --check still reports clean, cron script and aide package both present
